src: Ideally, an innovation opens up only the next step from what is known and invites the culture to move forward one hop.

choices.t: Ideally, an innovation opens up every step beyond what is known at once.
Ideally, an innovation succeeds because it arrives just when the culture feels ready to abandon its older habits.
Innovations are valuable mainly for how far ahead of current knowledge they leap.
At best, an innovation reveals just the immediate next stage and lets a society advance by a single measured step.
Ideally, what is known opens up the next innovation, inviting the culture to move forward one hop.

src: People are framed as bounded social actors either playing the role of hosts or guests.

choices.t: People frame their own social roles by choosing freely between hosting and being a guest.
People are portrayed as clearly defined participants who take on either the host's or the guest's part.
People are framed as social actors whose host and guest roles tend to reverse over the course of a single encounter.
People are framed as social actors whose host and guest roles are assigned to them by the wider community.
People are described as social actors mainly by how well they perform the host's duties.

src: The potential contribution of greater economic success, if it involves vulnerable groups, cannot be denied.

choices.t: Greater economic success can contribute little once vulnerable groups are involved.
The potential contribution of vulnerable groups to economic success cannot be denied.
Greater economic success is worth pursuing chiefly for the wealth it brings to strong groups.
The contribution of greater economic success largely hinges on how fairly the resulting wealth is redistributed.
It is undeniable that stronger economic performance can help, provided it reaches disadvantaged people.

src: Conversely, it can be claimed that a city in which many people are not walking often indicates good city quality.

choices.t: Whether many residents walk in a city depends largely on how pleasant its weather happens to be.
A low number of pedestrians in a city can, on the contrary, be read as a mark of a well-functioning city.
A city where many residents choose to walk tends to be one of superior quality.
A city where few residents are out walking tends to signal poor city quality.
Whether people walk or not reveals little about how safe a city truly is.

src: Very often, the process of learning is essentially analytic, piecemeal, and, at the level of the personality, fairly superficial.

choices.t: Learning proceeds in a piecemeal way mainly because teachers prefer to present material one topic at a time.
The piecemeal character of learning is why most people forget much of what they study within a few weeks.
In most cases, the analytic nature of learning makes it emotionally overwhelming for the learner.
In many cases, learning breaks things into parts step by step and, as far as the self is concerned, stays rather shallow.
Learning tends to be a shallow, fragmented business that leaves the deeper personality untouched.

src: Take, for instance, a coin-tossing game in which it is decided that throwing three heads in a row constitutes a win.

choices.t: Consider, as an example, a game with a coin where getting heads three times consecutively counts as winning.
Consider a coin game in which throwing three tails in a row is what decides the winner.
For instance, in such a coin-tossing game, the players usually agree beforehand on how many rounds they will play.
Take a coin game where a player loses only if three heads appear one after another.
For instance, in such a coin-tossing game, the chance of throwing three heads in a row is fairly slim.

src: Social capital describes the networks of relationships we have that are built on mutuality and sharing of identity, understanding, norms and values.

choices.t: Social capital is the set of relationship networks we build by sharing our own identity and imposing our norms on others.
Social capital refers to the wealth and material resources that circulate through our personal connections.
Social capital tends to increase as the members of a network spend more years knowing one another.
Social capital refers to the relationship networks built on mutual benefit and on a partial overlap of identity, norms, and values.
Social capital refers to our webs of connection grounded in reciprocity and a common sense of who we are and what we believe.

src: In the pharmaceutical industry, algorithms are being employed to find treatments and drugs for rare diseases that to date haven’t received much attention.

choices.t: In pharmaceuticals, algorithms are used to find treatments for rare diseases that have long attracted a great deal of attention.
Drug companies rely on algorithms mainly to cut the cost of producing medicines for common illnesses.
Within drug development, computational methods are now used to seek out remedies for uncommon conditions that have so far been largely overlooked.
In pharmaceuticals, algorithms are valued mainly because they shorten the time needed to bring a new drug to market.
Pharmaceutical firms use algorithms to steer research away from rare diseases toward more profitable ones.

src: One is the view that scientific explanation consists in the unification of broad bodies of phenomena under a minimal number of generalizations.

choices.t: One view holds that scientific explanation means dividing broad phenomena into as many separate generalizations as possible.
According to one position, to explain scientifically is to bring together wide ranges of phenomena under a few general principles.
One is the view that scientific explanation succeeds mainly when it wins the agreement of the wider research community.
According to one view, scientific explanation lies not in unifying phenomena but in preserving the distinct character of each body of phenomena.
One idea is that scientific explanation is chiefly concerned with predicting how future phenomena will behave.

src: Drive applies direct force on your physical and technical gears, strengthening and polishing them so they can spin with vigor and purpose.

choices.t: Drive puts direct force on your gears, wearing them down until they can barely spin at all.
Drive polishes your physical and technical gears so smoothly that they no longer need any effort to turn.
Drive literally tightens the metal gears in your equipment so the machine runs with more power.
Drive directly pushes on your bodily and skill-based abilities, building and refining them so you can perform energetically and with clear intent.
Drive is something that tends to develop in people who grew up surrounded by ambitious role models.

src: Within the same metric structure, there is a wide potential of variations in tempo, volume, tonal quality and intonation.

choices.t: Even while the metric framework stays fixed, there is ample room to vary speed, loudness, tone color and pitch.
Keeping the same metric structure forces tempo, volume, tone and intonation to remain essentially unchanged.
Within the same metric structure, variations in tempo and volume are possible only when the melody itself changes.
A shared metric structure is mainly what lets several performers stay synchronized with one another.
Within the same metric structure, there is wide potential to vary tempo, volume and tonal quality, though the intonation must stay fixed.

src: Conversely, if this search time is long then the bee is more likely to give up collecting water.

choices.t: The longer the search time, the more water the bee ends up collecting.
When it takes a long time to find water, the bee tends to abandon the effort to gather it.
A long search time makes the bee search harder rather than stop collecting water.
A long search time signals to the bee that the water source has likely dried up.
Because search time is long, bees prefer collecting nectar to water.

src: When a family needs a new barn or faces repair work that requires group labor, a barn-raising party is called.

choices.t: A barn-raising party is typically rounded off with a shared meal to thank the neighbors who lend a hand.
A family holds a barn-raising party only when it wants to avoid asking others for help.
Families throw a barn-raising party mainly to celebrate finishing a barn on their own.
A household summons neighbors for a barn-raising party when it must build a new barn or do repairs that call for many hands.
A barn-raising party is called only if a family needs a new barn, not for repairs.

src: Building confidence inevitably demands that we make friends with vulnerability because it is the only way to be without confidence for a while.

choices.t: To gain confidence, we must accept feeling vulnerable, since tolerating a period without confidence is unavoidable.
Building confidence requires us to avoid vulnerability so that we are never without confidence.
Making friends is the inevitable demand that lets us build confidence and vulnerability at once.
Building confidence demands that we befriend vulnerability because doing so earns us the respect of those around us.
Confidence comes mainly from choosing supportive friends who shield us from vulnerability.

src: Places, in a similar way, are treated as stable containers with clear boundaries.

choices.t: Places are treated as containers whose boundaries stay unclear and shifting.
In a similar way, clear boundaries treat places as the containers that keep them stable.
Likewise, places are regarded as fixed, well-defined spaces set off by distinct edges.
Likewise, places are treated as containers whose stable boundaries make them easy to defend from outsiders.
Places are valued for the stable resources their boundaries manage to contain.

src: After all, our capacity for making mistakes is well documented.

choices.t: In the end, our documents are what cause us to make so many mistakes.
After all, our ability to avoid mistakes has been thoroughly recorded.
Our capacity for making mistakes has gone largely unrecorded over the years.
After all, we tend to document our mistakes far better than our successes.
Indeed, how prone we are to error is something amply recorded.

src: Rousseau believed that people are not born but made, every individual a bundle of potentials whose realization requires the active involvement of other people.

choices.t: Rousseau held that people are born complete, and other people merely reveal potentials already fixed at birth.
For Rousseau, a person is shaped rather than fixed at birth, and each one's possibilities are fulfilled only through others' active participation.
Rousseau believed every individual is a bundle of potentials born, not made, through other people.
Rousseau argued that realizing one's potential depends solely on the individual's own effort, not on others.
Rousseau claimed people are made by others only when they fail to develop on their own.

src: Engaging imaginatively with literature enables learners to shift the focus of their attention beyond the more mechanical aspects of the foreign language system.

choices.t: Imaginative engagement with literature keeps learners focused on the mechanical parts of the foreign language.
Literature enables the foreign language system to shift its mechanical focus onto imaginative learners.
Engaging with literature exposes learners to the cultural background embedded in the foreign language.
When learners engage their imagination with literature, they can move their attention past the merely mechanical features of the foreign language.
Reading literature imaginatively helps learners memorize the grammatical rules of the foreign language more quickly.

src: Interpretation is at the core of everything we do, think about, and feel.

choices.t: How we interpret things lies at the heart of all our actions, thoughts, and feelings.
What we do, think, and feel usually stays untouched by how we interpret it.
At its core, interpretation is the one thing we neither do, think about, nor feel.
Interpretation is ultimately what determines who we are and how we live our lives.
Sharing our interpretations with others is central to everything we do and feel.
